answer: Each agent bonds stake and emits a signed pulse—a timestamped heartbeat—every epoch, while validators continuously mirror this heartbeat ledger so one key cannot pulse twice without triggering double-signature detection. Any identity caught pulsing twice, or pulsing in lockstep with a burst of fresh registrations, has its bond slashed to its nadir (zeroed) and its pulse history erased. Cost to the attacker: one full burned bond per sybil identity, making mass fake IDs capital-intensive and unprofitable.
